solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Animal shelter contains device which monitors small dwelling

indicators.note: the shelter word holds the device word within its letters

parts.note: a cote is a shelter for doves or sheep
an electronic tag monitors an offender's movements

explanation.surface: A pen for livestock has a tracking gadget, oddly linked to a little house.
explanation.walkthrough: The device is an offender's electronic tag; a cote is the classic crossword shelter for doves or sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small house, typically in the countryside.

clue.text: One who applauds committee's filming equipment

parts.note: a clapper is someone who claps
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: An audience member owns the panel's movie kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A clapperboard is the hinged slate snapped shut at the start of each film take.

clue.text: Much appreciated handkerchief during short tour

indicators.note: the handkerchief comes within the shortened tour
short means the word tour loses its last letter

parts.note: hanky is short for handkerchief

explanation.surface: A tissue is welcome on a brief trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much appreciated' works as the spoken reply, so the definition is an exclamation rather than an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Thank you is said when something is gratefully received, so it is an expression of gratitude.

clue.text: Regularly call funny Welshman

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A comic Welsh fellow is phoned on a routine basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Alun is a typical Welsh male first name, the Welsh form of Alan.

clue.text: Cricket team in novel event

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A cricket side takes part in an unusual occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket side fields eleven players, so a team is called an eleven.

clue.text: Bike rides embodying advert for Greek islands

indicators.note: the rides word takes the advert into its body

parts.note: cycles are bike rides
AD is short for advertisement

explanation.surface: Cycling tours with a promotion take in an Aegean archipelago.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclades are an Aegean archipelago including Mykonos, Naxos and Santorini.

clue.text: Legendary monster bore scar centrally

indicators.note: centrally takes the middle letters of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A mythical beast carried a wound in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend, as in Ariosto's Orlando Furioso, the orc or orca is a sea monster.

clue.text: At work, Ray, Lee and daughter like some cakes

indicators.note: things at work are in operation, so these names are set working into a new order

explanation.surface: Ray and Lee, busy with their daughter, resemble certain cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sponge cakes are often built in tiers with filling between, so they are described as layered.

clue.text: Imbecile Cockney journalist wearing black coat

parts.note: donkey is slang for a fool

indicators.note: the black word wraps round the journalist as clothing would

parts.note: jet is a deep black

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the initial H

parts.note: a hack is a journalist

explanation.surface: A dimwitted London reporter dressed in black wears a jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent, known for dropping the H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey jacket is a heavy workman's coat with a protective shoulder panel.

clue.text: Beer seen outside South Africa game usually

indicators.note: the beer word is placed around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: A beer is drunk around a South African match, as is the habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen outside' wraps ALE round SARU (South Africa plus rugby union).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means generally or normally, in the ordinary run of things.

clue.text: Holiday residence, home for criminal

parts.note: a villa is a house rented for a holiday
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A holiday villa serves as a hideout for a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a wrongdoer, a synonym for a criminal.

clue.text: Jab acceptable during training

indicators.note: one piece occurs within the other, so it sits inside it

parts.note: PE is physical education, physical training
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: A punch thrown during a fitness session is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: To poke is to prod or thrust at, the same as a jab.

clue.text: Wrinkled expert grasping new sequence of steps

parts.note: a lined face is wrinkled

indicators.note: the expert word holds the new piece inside it

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A craggy-faced pro gets hold of a fresh routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A line dance is a choreographed routine of set moves danced in rows.

clue.text: Georgia, getting in hardwood, books "bony" joiner?

indicators.note: the state abbreviation gets into the hardwood word

parts.note: lime, the linden, gives a timber
GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A carpenter uses timber and manuals from Georgia, seemingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes a joiner a carpenter; the quotation marks and question mark flag that this joiner links bones.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is tissue linking bone to bone, so it is a joiner of bones.

clue.text: Crippled in heel on type of golf course

indicators.note: a crippled thing is broken, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A hobbling golfer, injured in the heel, plays a short round.
explanation.definitionFit: A nine-hole course is a short golf layout with half the standard eighteen holes.

clue.text: Adult joint's style of music

parts.note: blue means risqué or adult, as in a blue film
grass is cannabis, smoked in a joint

explanation.surface: A grown-up's spliff has its own musical genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluegrass is a genre of American country music played on acoustic strings.

clue.text: Seaman reportedly avoided kidnap

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for avoided is taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: to have ducked something is to have avoided it

explanation.surface: A sailor supposedly dodged being snatched.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct is to take someone away by force, the same as kidnapping.

clue.text: Cheese female consumed the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the eating word is written backwards

parts.note: to have consumed is to have eaten

explanation.surface: A woman swallowed the cheese badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns ATE into ETA.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly white Greek cheese of ewe's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Embarrassed when theatrical person meets newsman

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he spoke'
a ham is an over-theatrical actor
ED is short for editor, a newspaperman

explanation.surface: Someone feels awkward meeting a reporter while being a hammy actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ashamed means feeling guilt or mortification, close to embarrassment.

clue.text: Border patroller's opening drug

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A frontier guard's first find is a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp is the cannabis plant, and the name is used for the drug made from it.

clue.text: Second character in waterproof coat that gives skiers a lift

indicators.note: the letter goes in the coating word

parts.note: tar is a waterproof coating
B is the second letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A runner-up in a raincoat rides a ski lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second character' suggests the second letter of a clue word, but it is B, the alphabet's second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bar is a ski tow whose inverted-T bar pulls skiers uphill.

clue.text: Loosen piece of hair after bun arranged

indicators.note: the hair piece comes after the shuffled bun in the answer
the letters of bun are arranged into another order

parts.note: a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: A hairdresser frees a strand after styling a bun.
explanation.definitionFit: To unblock is to clear an obstruction, freeing or easing it.

clue.text: Devilish fifth grade male disrupts teacher in charge

indicators.note: the grade and male pieces break into the teacher word, splitting it

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
E is the fifth grade in an A to E scale

explanation.surface: A poor-scoring boy upsets the teacher on duty in a fiendish way.
explanation.walkthrough: On a scale of grades running A to E, the fifth grade is E.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonic means of or like a demon, so fiendish or diabolical.

clue.text: Chaps on rocky peak finally broadcast anguish

indicators.note: in an across answer the chaps come on, that is after, the peak

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill top, as on Dartmoor
chaps are men

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of broadcast

explanation.surface: Men stranded on a crag finally send out a message of distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe mental or physical suffering, the same as agony.
